notes: Curated Reader passages: verse references selected by reproducible gate scoring (tools/import_oshb_reader.mjs) from the pinned OSHB corpus, grouped by lesson gate and tier.

Tiers: strict = all graded morphology in scope at the verse's own gateLesson, <=1 unknown non-proper content lexeme; guided = all morphology in scope, <=3 unknown non-proper content lexemes (marked); challenge (reworked in task 13a) = presented at a LOWER gate than the verse's own natural maxGrammarLesson, with 1-3 tokens sharing exactly one future feature TYPE (one shared bbhLesson value, e.g. "2 Past Narrative forms, Lesson 35") exempted above that lower gate, plus <=2 unknown non-proper content lexemes overall; every challenge entry carries a `challengeNote` naming the future feature. Hidden by default in the Reader UI (challenge toggle), unlike strict/guided.

CURATION METHOD (Phase 2 PR D): for each of the 10 gate buckets in tools/import_oshb_reader.mjs's bucketOf() (9-14, 15-19, 20-22, 23-27, 28-31, 32-34, 35-38, 39-41, 42-44, 45-50), up to 4 strict + 2 guided verses were hand-picked from that bucket's candidate list (node tools/import_oshb_reader.mjs --report, plus an ad hoc ranking script used only during authoring to enumerate/sort candidates), preferring in order: (a) verses from Genesis 1, 3, 22, 37, 38, 47, 50 (our own narrative-domain picks, independent of the textbook's own curated reading sequence), (b) shorter verses (lower tokenCount), (c) contiguous verse runs where the ranked candidate list offered one (e.g. Gen 36:25-28, a 4-verse contiguous strict run at the L33 gate; Gen 10:16-17 and 25:14-15 pairs). `gateLesson` always equals the verse's own `scores.maxGrammarLesson` here because every selected verse is strict or guided (Genesis, under this policy, produced zero 'challenge'-tier verses corpus-wide as of this pass — see the PR D report; the challenge tier is fully implemented in tools/import_oshb_reader.mjs and would populate here if a future gate-map/vocab refinement produced one).

REPRODUCIBILITY: `scores` for every entry below is checked byte-for-byte (JSON-equal) against a FRESH run of importGenesis() by tools/validate_bbh_reader_data.mjs — any gate-map, override-table, or importer change that shifts a verse's score fails validation here until selections.json is re-curated or the drifted entries are removed.
Populated in Phase 2 PR D alongside tools/import_oshb_reader.mjs. Empty in PR A by design.

READER BOOK EXPANSION (task: multi-book expansion, after PR H): the importer (tools/import_oshb_reader.mjs) now scores 8 books — Gen, Ruth, Jonah, Exod, Deut, Judg, 1Sam, 2Sam — over the same pinned OSHB checkout. The 52 pre-existing Genesis selections above are UNCHANGED (same ids/scores; re-verified byte-for-byte against a fresh import after the gate-map/override-table updates below). 26 new selections were added from the 7 new books: (a) thin-bucket fill for gate buckets 15-19/23-27/28-31, which previously had only 1-2 Genesis strict candidates, drawing exclusively from non-Genesis books, shortest tokenCount first; (b) up to 2 strict + 1 guided per new book, chosen from that book's single richest gate bucket (all 7 landed in bucket 35-38, the Qal wayyiqtol/past-narrative gate — the natural backbone of Biblical Hebrew narrative prose, so unsurprisingly every narrative book's deepest candidate pool). No challenge-tier verses were found in ANY of the 8 books (tier definition: exactly one clearly-identified near-future-lesson token, all others in scope) — same null result as the original Genesis-only pass; the challenge tier remains fully implemented and ready to populate if a future gate-map/override refinement produces a match. Selection picking was scripted (scratchpad/curate_reader.mjs, not part of the shipped tool chain) directly against a fresh importReaderCorpus() run, so every new entry's scores are trivially exact-reproducible by construction. LEMMA_OVERRIDES was extended with entries audited from the combined top-60 unresolved Strong's numbers across all 8 books (tools/import_oshb_reader.mjs's own header comment there documents 3 entries — אֱלֹהִים 430, אֶרֶץ 776, צִוָּה 6680 — that were found to genuinely match a CSV row but were deliberately withheld because adding them drifts 5 of the 52 fixed Genesis selections' scores). Coverage-gap count across all 8 books is 0 (unchanged) — gate-map.json needed no new entries beyond what Phase 2 PR D had already authored (its existing per-POS-letter safety-net catch-alls already cover every OSHB morph code observed in the 7 new books).

CHALLENGE TIER REWORK (task 13a, 2026-08-09 addenda "matcher fixes"/"challenge tier rework"/"underline noise"): two matcher bugs were fixed in tools/import_oshb_reader.mjs's classifyToken() — (1) OSHB gentilic nouns (Ng: the Hivite/Arkite/Sinite/Philistine/etc. nation-name family) are now pn-class (excluded from unknownContentLexemes, isProperName:true, plus a distinct isGentilic/gent:true flag), matching how proper names (Np) were already handled — previously a verse full of untaught gentilic names (e.g. Gen 10:16-17) was wrongly counted as several unknown content words; (2) compound-token vocab matching now also checks a pure-function-word token's own core segment (e.g. the object-marker segment of ו/את) against the vocab index even when that token has no N/V/A content segment, so taught particle vocabulary (את, CSV L15) surfaces its vocabLesson for display/underline purposes instead of silently reading null. The freeze on 3 previously-withheld LEMMA_OVERRIDES entries (אֱלֹהִים 430 CSV L3, אֶרֶץ 776 CSV L9, צִוָּה 6680 CSV L35) was also lifted. Re-scoring the whole 8-book corpus with these fixes changed 10 of the 78 pre-existing selections above: reader-gen-10-16 and reader-gen-10-17 improved guided->strict (unknownContentLexemes 3->0, the exact Gen 10:17 screenshot case); reader-gen-1-1 and reader-gen-24-4 improved guided->strict (430/776 override additions); reader-gen-10-20 and reader-2sam-5-18 stayed guided but dropped one unknownContentLexemes; reader-gen-50-12/reader-gen-38-2/reader-gen-7-5 stayed strict but dropped to 0 unknownContentLexemes. No selection's tier got worse. All other 69 selections' scores/tier/gateLesson are byte-identical to their pre-13a values (reader-deut-6-4 also changed, but from a SEPARATE, unrelated fix — see the large-letter tokenizer note below).

The challenge tier itself was separately reworked (docs' "challenge tier rework" addendum): the ORIGINAL definition ("exactly one near-future-lesson token, <=3 unknown content lexemes") could structurally never fire (its own threshold was a strict subset of guided's, so guided always claimed the verse first — zero challenge candidates were ever found in any of the 8 books). scoreVerse() in tools/import_oshb_reader.mjs now computes challenge-eligibility as an INDEPENDENT diagnostic (`scores.challenge`), never overriding the primary strict/guided `tier` — an early draft that checked challenge before strict/guided (the only way to make the tighter threshold reachable) flipped 60+ of the 78 pre-existing selections into "challenge" purely because every ordinary short clause has "one token at the single highest lesson (its main verb) plus a lower baseline", which is completely normal sentence structure, not a rare/noteworthy shape. Keeping the two independent means a verse's primary tier is unaffected by whether it ALSO happens to be challenge-eligible; a curator opts a specific verse INTO the challenge tier explicitly (as done below). Two curation-quality floors beyond the doc's three numeric conditions: the lower gate G must be >= lesson 9 (bucketOf()'s own curation floor — below that is bare pronoun/article/preposition connective tissue with no real "baseline" to preview against), and the gap (maxGrammarLesson - G) must be >= 10 (so "future feature" means a meaningfully distant course unit, e.g. Past Narrative or Numerals, not just the next lesson or two over). Scanning all 8 books found 293 challenge-eligible verses across gate buckets 9-14 through 35-38 (none in 39-41/42-44/45-50 — see tools/import_oshb_reader.mjs --report's "Challenge-eligible candidates" section); 8 were curated below (reader-ch-* ids), one or two per bucket, spread across Gen/1Sam/Exod/2Sam and across feature types (Qal/Piel wayyiqtol, Hitpael wayyiqtol, Imperative, numerals), chosen for clean short clauses with a verified challengeNote.

LARGE-LETTER TOKENIZER FIX (task 13a, found while authoring wooden translations): OSHB marks the two traditionally-enlarged Masoretic letters in the Shema (Deut 6:4 — שְׁמַע's ע and אֶחָד's ד) with a <seg type="x-large"> tag NESTED inside the <w> element itself, which tools/import_oshb_reader.mjs's original regex-based tokenizer (requiring a <w> body with no "<" at all) silently failed to match — both tokens vanished from the stream rather than erroring. This is the ONLY nested-tag-inside-<w> case anywhere in the 8-book corpus (grep-verified: exactly 2 <seg type="x-large"> occurrences total, both in this one verse). Fixed in W_RE/NESTED_SEG_RE (flattens the nested <seg> back to plain text, byte-identical to the unmarked word) with the identical fix mirrored in validate_bbh_reader_data.mjs's independent extractRawTokenDisplays(). reader-deut-6-4 (already a curated selection) went from 4 tokens/gate L31 (missing "Hear" and "one" entirely) to the correct 6 tokens/gate L45 (אֶחָד "one" is a numeral, gate-mapped to L45) — still tier:"strict" (1 unknown content lexeme, was 0). No other selection or verse in the corpus is affected (the only other <seg type="x-large"> instance is the matching אֶחָד in the same verse).

TASK #24 STAGE B (Reader prose expansion, 2026-08-09): the importer (tools/import_oshb_reader.mjs) now scores 13 books (task #24 stage A added Josh/1Kgs/2Kgs/Esth/Ps to the prior 8). The 86 pre-existing selections above are UNCHANGED (same ids/scores; re-verified byte-for-byte against a fresh import). 12 new selections were added from the 4 new PROSE books (Josh/1Kgs/2Kgs/Esth — Psalms is stage C's job, challenge-tier poetry only, not curated here): 2 strict + 1 guided per book, chosen for (a) short (5-17 token) verses that score well at an honest gate, (b) thin-bucket fill where a good candidate existed (20-22, 23-27, 39-41, 42-44 all gained entries; 15-19/28-31/32-34 were left untouched — no strong short/pedagogical candidate was found there in these 4 books, per the "do not force it" instruction), and (c) pedagogically attractive narrative regions where the scores actually supported it: Josh 1 (commissioning)/Josh 24 (covenant renewal) flank the famous but non-scoring 1:9/24:15; 1Kgs 2 (David's charge to Solomon, "be strong")/1Kgs 3 (Solomon's judgment)/1Kgs 19 (Elijah told to anoint Elisha, bridging into the Elisha material); 2Kgs 2/5 (Elisha's Jericho-waters and Naaman narratives); Esth 2 (Mordecai introduced)/Esth 4 (the Esther-Mordecai-Hathach relay immediately surrounding "for such a time as this", 4:14, which does not itself score strict/guided — its neighbors 4:9/4:10/4:12/4:15/4:17 do). No new LEMMA_OVERRIDES entries were added (every selected verse already reached its tier without one; task 13a's own experience — 3 known-safe overrides drifting 5 Genesis scores — argued for leaving the override table untouched when not strictly needed). All 12 new `wooden` translations are author-drafted, `woodenStatus:"draft"` — NOT YET independently reviewed against token morphology; that is stage D's job, same convention as task 13a's original draft pass. `tools/check_release.mjs` check5b passage count updated 86->98; validator/generator both green, gen twice byte-identical, and the 86 pre-existing selections' scores/tier/gateLesson are untouched.

TASK #24 STAGE C (Psalms challenge-tier poetry, 2026-08-09): 8 challenge-tier-ONLY selections curated from Psalms (reader-ch-ps-* ids) — the first poetry in the Reader corpus. Every entry uses the SAME scoreVerse() challenge diagnostic as the original 8 challenge showcases (task 13a): unknownContentLexemes<=2, allMapped, a single lower "in-scope" gate G>=9 with (maxGrammarLesson-G)>=10, 1-3 tokens at the verse's own max lesson. Of the user-suggested candidate pool (Ps 1, 23, 100, 117, 121, 150), only Psalm 121 produced natural challenge-eligible verses (121:2, 121:8 — both included); every verse individually checked in Ps 1/23/100/117/150 either scored ordinary strict/guided already (no >=10-lesson gap above a single feature) or had too many unknown content lexemes, so 6 of the 8 entries substitute equally famous, equally short psalm verses that DO score into the challenge shape: Ps 95:3 ("a great God is YHWH"), Ps 113:5-6 ("Who is like YHWH our God, who makes high to sit... who makes low to see"), Ps 114:1 (the Exodus-Hallel opening, "When Yisrael went out from Mitsrayim"), Ps 130:4 ("with you is forgiveness"), Ps 146:1 ("Praise Yah! Praise, O my soul, YHWH"). Every challengeNote leads with a plain genre label ("Poetry — Psalm N. Verse structure and word order differ from prose narrative.") before the usual future-feature sentence, reusing the EXISTING challenge-note UI (js/ui/reader.js's reader-challenge-note box) — no new UI mechanism was added; the badge/caption machinery already fit. All 8 wooden translations are author-drafted fresh from the Hebrew, woodenStatus:"draft" (stage D reviews), following the corpus's existing house style (YHWH for the divine name, Hebrew-style transliterated proper names, literal Hebrew word order preserved even where it reads as poetic inversion — e.g. Ps 95:3's verbless "for a great God is YHWH"). No LEMMA_OVERRIDES entries added. The 98 pre-existing selections are byte-for-byte unchanged (re-verified against a fresh regeneration).
